name: Amdo Tibetan
sweep_summary: Amdo Tibetan is not in the catalog. The sweep list holds one item, Caplow's 2009 UCSB dissertation (607 pp.) on stress and Tibetan tonogenesis, which uses Rebkong Amdo as one of its two atonal source varieties; it is ProQuest-restricted (record opened, no abstract, no free copy; UCSB ADRL has no record; search engines and S2/OpenAlex/CORE/BASE/OATD were blocked or rate-limited from our machine), so it stays high-priority to acquire (Harvard HOLLIS link on file). The author's follow-up, Caplow 2016 LTBA 39(2) 'Reconstructing stress in Proto-Tibetan: Evidence from Balti and Rebkong Amdo' (not in the sweep list), gives the same data in a published form; only its abstract was reachable (paywalled at John Benjamins, OpenAlex closed), saved with the page HTML and OpenAlex record under with. That abstract is the best first-hand statement obtained: Rebkong Amdo disyllabic nouns/adjectives/numerals carry stress on the second (final) syllable; disyllabic verbs are never σ2-stressed and on limited data are σ1-stressed. On-disk secondary sources agree (Tournadre & Suzuki 2023 sec. 7.3.3, 9.5.6; Lim 2018 sec. 1.3.3.1; Caplow 2016 HL Balti paper fn. 3 gives Rebkong Amdo [xso.'ra] 'sickle'). Recommended acquisition: the 2016 LTBA full text (pp. 180-221) first, then the 2009 dissertation (pp. 527-528 per Lim for the reconstruction).

new_statements.quote: For both Balti and Rebkong Amdo, stress falls on the second syllable (σ2) of disyllabic non-verbs — nouns, adjectives, and numerals. [...] Disyllabic verbs are never stressed on σ2. For Balti, robust evidence shows that they are stressed on the first syllable (σ1). Limited data for Rebkong Amdo suggests the same pattern. Thus σ1 stress is tentatively reconstructed for verbs in Proto-Tibetan.
new_statements.citation: Caplow, Nancy J. 2016. Reconstructing stress in Proto-Tibetan: Evidence from Balti and Rebkong Amdo. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 39(2): 180-221. DOI 10.1075/ltba.39.2.01cap
new_statements.locator: Abstract (publisher landing page https://www.jbe-platform.com/content/journals/10.1075/ltba.39.2.01cap, fetched sources 2026-09-17); full text paywalled
new_statements.reading: First-hand (author's own acoustic/perceptual study) statement for Rebkong Amdo Tibetan: in disyllabic nouns, adjectives and numerals stress is on the second = final syllable; disyllabic verbs are not final-stressed and, on limited data, are initial-stressed. So Amdo (Rebkong) has category-conditioned word stress: final in non-verbs, initial in verbs. This is an abstract-level statement, not the body text; the full data tables and any statement about longer words remain unread. Secondary corroboration on file: Tournadre & Suzuki 2023 sec. 7.3.3 and 9.5.6 (Amdo atonal; Caplow and others hold that Amdo has a stress opposition, secondary in the system) and Lim 2018 sec. 1.3.3.1 (summarising Caplow 2009: non-verbs *σσ́, verbs *σ́σ from Balti and Rebkong Amdo).

sources.quote: For both Balti and Rebkong Amdo, stress falls on the second syllable (σ2) of disyllabic non-verbs — nouns, adjectives, and numerals. Through the method of “historical comparative prosody”, σ2 stress is likewise reconstructed for disyllabic non-verbs in Proto-Tibetan. Disyllabic verbs are never stressed on σ2. For Balti, robust evidence shows that they are stressed on the first syllable (σ1). Limited data for Rebkong Amdo suggests the same pattern.
sources.note: Rebkong Amdo (a conservative, atonal Amdo variety): disyllabic nouns, adjectives and numerals are stressed on the second (final) syllable; disyllabic verbs are never σ2-stressed and, on limited data, appear σ1-stressed as in Balti. Stress is thus lexical-category-conditioned (final for non-verbs, initial for verbs). Abstract only; the body (pp. 180-221) with the Amdo word lists and acoustic evidence was not reachable. Consistent with the single Rebkong Amdo form in the on-disk Caplow 2016 Himalayan Linguistics Balti paper, fn. 3: [xso.'ra] 'sickle' (final stress).
